elements.content: Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

items.definition: the gradual loss of words or grammatical structures in a language over time.
items.example: Some experts are concerned about linguistic decay caused by rapid texting.

items.definition: reciprocal action or influence between two or more people.
items.example: Face-to-face interaction is essential for maintaining social skills.

items.definition: consisting of one syllable (often used to describe short, unhelpful answers).
items.example: He gave a monosyllabic reply when I asked how his day was.

items.definition: the amount of information that working memory can hold at one time.
items.example: Deep conversation requires a higher cognitive load than simple messaging.

items.definition: fluent or persuasive speaking or writing.
items.example: His eloquence made him a very effective public speaker.

items.definition: the total number of different words a person knows and uses.
items.example: Reading diverse books is the best way to expand your vocabulary range.

items.definition: the state of being separate from others.
items.example: Physical isolation is highly linked to cognitive decline in older seniors.

items.definition: a subtle difference in meaning, expression, or sound.
items.example: A rich vocabulary allows you to express every small nuance of emotion.

items.definition: losing focus on a task or conversation because of a digital device.
items.example: Digital distraction is often cited as a cause for shorter real-life conversations.

items.definition: relating to relationships or communication between people.
items.example: The company is looking for candidates with strong interpersonal skills.
